name: IT team · M1 demo outcome → capture feedback and re-forecast M2/M3
description:
Owner: ProjectManager (management duty). Wakes **2026-11-21T16:00Z**, two hours after the M1 demo slot (Fri 21 Nov 14:00).

## Why this card exists
The agile rule is *demo, then re-plan*. After the M1 walkthrough nobody owned "write down what management saw, what they said, and what that does to M2/M3 dates". Without this card the feedback is verbal and the M2 (25 Nov) / M3 (27 Nov) forecasts stay unexamined — a silent slip.

## Inputs to read first
- `b9aaf03c` — M1 bring-up card (demo evidence: commands, container health, HTTP status, screenshot).
- `2506f948` — M1 demo go/no-go: whether the live audience happened or the walkthrough was **recorded** (default C if no audience was named by 20 Nov 12:00).
- `299d12ce` (M2, wakes 23 Nov 09:00) and `140668fe` (M3, wakes 24 Nov 09:00) — the two forecasts to re-baseline.

## Do
1. Record the **outcome** of the demo in one paragraph on this card: what was shown, on what environment, who saw it (or "recorded, no live audience").
2. Record the **feedback** verbatim as a bullet list — including "no issues raised". Never leave it implicit.
3. Re-forecast **M2 and M3 dates** against that feedback. If scope moved, present it as a trade-off (date or scope), never as absorbed work.
4. If a feedback item is a **new feature**, do not fold it into M2/M3: create a separate card and put it on the backlog behind M3.

## Acceptance
A comment on this card containing: demo outcome, feedback bullets, and either "M2/M3 dates unchanged, because …" or the new dates. Then close the card.

## Not in this card
Re-running the demo, fixing anything found, rescheduling the team. Those become their own cards.

## PM note — 2026-11-19 shift #5 (turn 3): this card has two inputs, not one

Your 21 Nov 16:00Z wake assumes a demo happened. As of now that is only one of three possible states, and the other two matter more than the happy path. Read `4f055e99` (*M1 demo NO-GO branch*, 10:30Z) and `101588b6` (rehearsal, 09:00Z) before you write anything.

**Case 1 — rehearsal said `GO` and the demo ran.** Do exactly what this card already says: capture management's feedback verbatim, then re-forecast M2 (`299d12ce`, Mon 23 Nov) and M3 (`140668fe`, Tue 24 Nov) from that feedback — never silently absorb a scope change.

**Case 2 — rehearsal said `NO-GO`.** There is no feedback to capture. Instead: record the failure as the demo outcome, state which of M2/M3 now moves and by how much, and propose the replacement slot that `4f055e99` raised (`2506f948`). Do not carry the M2/M3 dates forward as if M1 had passed — that is the one failure mode that makes a re-forecast worthless.

**Case 3 — `GO` but the room was empty** (no management sign-off confirmed by the 20 Nov 12:00 deadline on `2506f948`). Then the default applies: the walkthrough was recorded by `def4ce38` at 11:00Z, and this card must report *"demo delivered asynchronously, no feedback yet, M2/M3 dates unchanged"* plus a wake to collect the feedback later. Absence of an audience is not a failure of the increment — do not report it as one.

**In all three cases:** the DoD for M1 is *not* "demo ran". It is code reviewed + tests green + deployed to the demo environment + demo script written + acceptance criteria demonstrated. Say for each of those five whether it is met, unknown, or not met. A milestone is never closed because a meeting occurred.
